<SUMMARY>The global AI infrastructure sector is experiencing significant investment and technological advancements, though public concerns about resource consumption are rising. Geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding AI chip export controls and critical mineral supply chains, are driving national strategies for diversification. The ongoing conflict in West Asia continues to impact global markets and energy security.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>Persistent constraints in TSMC's 3nm wafer supply for AI customers pose a critical vulnerability. The Democratic Republic of Congo’s cobalt export ban threatens the global EV battery supply chain. Public sentiment in the United States is wary of the AI-driven data center boom, raising concerns about electricity bills and potential job losses. Taiwan is considering tighter controls on AI chip exports to China, potentially altering supply dynamics. The escalation of conflict in West Asia and its impact on global markets and energy flows, specifically via the Strait of Hormuz, remains a significant red flag.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:** OpenAI banned two clusters of China-linked accounts for anti-AI influence campaigns, which were generating content criticizing AI data centers and President Trump's tariffs. Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd signed power supply agreements with PLN for its Indonesia AI data center project. The Philippines joined the US Pax Silica initiative and plans a $10 billion tech hub with a 99-year lease. SK Chairman Chey is eyeing Japan for AI infrastructure expansion. Polymatech established an Asia-Pacific Advanced Manufacturing Hub in Singapore. Chinese chip foundry United Nova plans to invest US$3 billion in AI power and optical interconnects.

**Americas:** A KKR-led group launched a new company with over $10 billion in committed capital to finance AI infrastructure, partnering with Nvidia and Vistra. ZincFive Inc., a specialized battery maker supplying data centers, agreed to go public through a merger with a SparkLabs SPAC at a $600 million pre-money valuation. Unisys earned the Dell Technologies 2026 Global Alliances Americas Data Center Partner of the Year award. Bechtel landed the first phase of construction on Micron’s $100 billion semiconductor fabs.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Asia:** Ennostar qualified Veeco’s new LUMINA®+ MOCVD system for advanced product applications. TSMC’s 3nm wafer supply remains constrained for AI customers, even as monthly production reached a milestone of 175,000 units. NVIDIA’s Feynman AI Chip is poised to break the CoWoS size barrier, with TSMC's next-generation packaging technology, CoPoS, expected to enter mass production in 2028. Taiwan is weighing tighter rules for AI chip exports to China and is mulling curbs on AI chip exports to China to align with the US. A Chinese startup reported finding a cheaper way to make photonic chips.

**Americas:** The global foundry market hit a record $47.95 billion in Q1 2026, with TSMC expanding its market share to 72%. Google tapped Samsung for next-gen AI chip production. Forge Nano secured a semiconductor wafer fab equipment order from a leading photonics technology company for commercial integrated photonics manufacturing.

**Europe:** Europe is pursuing a new AI chip dream.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Americas:** Midland Exploration Inc. identified several lake bottom copper anomalies from its 2025 high-resolution survey completed on the Lac Bernard project. Labrador Gold will host an investor webinar on the Mariposa Gold Project in Yukon’s White Gold District. Energy Fuels expects to achieve its full-year uranium production guidance by mid-year, with an anticipated 1.6 million pounds of finished U3O8 produced from January through June 2026 from its U.S. uranium operations. The U.S. House of Representatives passed the U.S. Dominance Act, authorizing equity investment, co-financing, and U.S.-priority offtake for allied critical mineral projects, and defining "processed" to include awaruite, a natural nickel-iron-cobalt alloy. Jim Rickards highlighted a June 30 deadline connected to what could be the largest mineral haul in U.S. history.

**Africa:** The Democratic Republic of Congo’s cobalt export ban is expected to cause trouble for the world's EV battery supply.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:** Taiwan is considering tighter rules for AI chip exports to China.

**Americas:** The U.S. House of Representatives passed the U.S. Dominance Act, which relates to critical minerals.

**Europe:** G7 allies will seek to narrow differences with President Trump at a summit in France.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Asia:** Taiwan test fired HIMARS toward China. Worries are mounting over US missile supplies.

**Americas:** Swarmer Inc., a drone autonomy software company, has supported more than 100,000 real-world combat missions in Ukraine since April 2024. Retail traders are dumping Big Tech to raise ‘dry powder’ to buy SpaceX.

**Europe:** Mercedes-Benz partnered with TYTAN Technologies to develop vehicle-based systems that detect and shoot down hostile drones, built on its G-Class SUV platform.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>The global AI sector is experiencing rapid expansion, marked by significant infrastructure investments and technological advancements in chip production and packaging. However, this growth is coupled with increased geopolitical tensions, supply chain vulnerabilities in critical minerals and advanced chips, and public scrutiny over resource consumption. Nations are actively pursuing strategies to secure critical mineral supplies and diversify their AI supply chains, highlighted by Taiwan's potential export controls. The ongoing conflict in West Asia continues to influence global markets and energy security, demanding close monitoring and adaptive strategies from international actors.</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>Indian industrial groups Reliance, Vedanta, and Adani are among ten companies expressing interest in developing facilities to process Andhra Pradesh state’s significant reserves of rare-earth minerals, aligning with India's drive to cut China rare earth dependence. Hidden AI India winners have added $48 billion, with Indian industrial companies experiencing significant growth by supplying components for data centers, including transformers, cooling systems, and cables. Indian businesses are optimistic about FY27, with telecom, defense, metals, and banking seen driving growth, and AI boosting telecom infrastructure. Uncompensable heat stress (UHS) emerged during the monsoon season in India. Prabhudas Lilladher cut its Nifty target to 26,449 due to global market turmoil and El Nino, listing 16 high conviction stock picks. Sensex ended 150.63 points lower, or 0.20 percent, at 73,832.55, while the Nifty closed at 23,161.60, down 53.35 points or 0.23 percent.</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>Iran declared the Middle East war ceasefire "practically meaningless" following fresh US strikes, responding with attacks across the region. President Trump stated he "may keep going" with strikes and that Iran "will have to pay the price" for taking too long to negotiate a deal. Iran announced strikes on US-linked sites before they occurred. President Trump later stated he "cancels Iran strikes, says Tehran has 'approved' talks." Speculation arose about the US having moved 100 million barrels of oil out of Hormuz, though the maths does not appear to hold up. Kuwait joined a growing number of Middle Eastern oil and gas producers in shipping energy cargoes in dark mode through the Strait of Hormuz. Neurovia AI participated in the 2026 UAE Data Center Infrastructure & Cloud Summit as an Official AI Infrastructure Partner, highlighting NeuroStream™ and new leadership. AI is set to consume up to 600 billion gallons of water by 2030, driven by rising energy consumption from data centers. The Iran war is adding to the AI boom, increasing demand for gas turbines, according to Siemens Energy. US-Iran tensions could shape world markets. The geopolitics of China-Israel trade and investment are being observed. The impact of the Middle East conflict on Asia-Pacific power markets is noted. A UAE oil break exposed a deepening Saudi rift. Duke Robotics strengthened its leadership team with Yiftach Kleinman as CEO, who previously worked at Israeli defense companies.</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The confluence of an expanding AI industry, ongoing geopolitical conflicts in West Asia, and a global scramble for critical resources defines the immediate future. The push for AI infrastructure will continue to drive investments and technological innovation, but will also exacerbate competition for energy and minerals, alongside increasing public scrutiny over environmental impact. The volatile situation in West Asia threatens to further disrupt global supply chains and energy markets, demanding close monitoring and adaptive strategies from international actors.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
